summary: TimeTrack is a web application for tracking work time and activities, backed by an Internet Computer (ICP) Motoko canister. Authenticated users log in via Internet Identity, set up a basic user profile, and then manage daily time entries (work, vacation, on-call/astreinte) with detailed time slots plus meal and travel time. The app also supports attaching daily media (photos and audio recordings) to calendar days, maintaining a work journal with notes and photo attachments, viewing monthly dashboard analytics (cards + charts), and exporting reports as CSV or printable PDF (PDF data produced by the backend and rendered via browser print). The backend includes role-based access control (admin/user/guest), per-user filtering for most reads, counts for vacation and on-call days, and a blob-storage mixin for managing external blob lifecycles on ICP.
architectural_notes: Frontend is React + TypeScript using @tanstack/react-query for data fetching/caching; backend calls are wrapped in dedicated query/mutation hooks (useQueries.ts) with explicit cache invalidation.
Authentication uses DFINITY Internet Identity via @dfinity/auth-client, exposed through a React Context provider (InternetIdentityProvider). Delegations are configured for ~30 days TTL.
Backend integration uses an “actor” abstraction created per identity (useActor). When the identity changes, the app invalidates/refetches all non-actor queries to prevent cross-user cache leakage.
Motoko backend is a single canister actor (main.mo) storing data in in-memory Map structures (time entries, journal entries, daily media, user profiles, files).

Role-based access control is implemented in a dedicated module (authorization/access-control.mo): first registered principal becomes admin; others become user; anonymous is guest. Most canister methods require #user permission and enforce owner/admin checks on updates/deletes.

Dates are exchanged as nanosecond timestamps (Time.Time / bigint); frontend converts JS milliseconds to nanoseconds via `date.getTime() * 1_000_000`. Work times are stored as minutes-from-midnight integers (also bigint in frontend bindings).

Daily media uses an ExternalBlob abstraction with direct URLs and optional upload progress callbacks; the backend includes a blob-storage mixin for gateway authorization, blob GC/pruning, and cashier cycle refills.
UI uses TailwindCSS (OKLCH tokens, dark mode via class) and shadcn/ui components; notifications use sonner toasts; charts use recharts.
Reports include client-side CSV generation and a backend-assisted PDF report data generator; the PDF itself is produced client-side by opening a new window and calling `window.print()`.
There is an ICP HTTP outcalls helper (http-outcalls/outcall.mo) providing GET/POST with transform functions and fixed cycle budgeting (not shown as wired into main canister in provided files).
known_issues: Backend period/date helpers are stubbed: `estJourSemaine` always returns true and `extraireMois/extraireAnnee/extraireSemaine` all return 0. This breaks weekly/monthly filtering in backend totals and PDF generation (`genererDonneesRapportPdf`, `calculerTotauxPourMois`, `calculerTotauxPourSemaine`) and makes weekday logic incorrect server-side.

PDF report data formatting in backend uses raw `entry.date.toText()` (nanoseconds int) and raw minute values labeled as “h” (hours). The generated table/total units are likely incorrect or not human-friendly.

Potential ID collision/overwrite risk: create endpoints (`enregistrerJournee`, `enregistrerJournal`, `enregistrerMediaQuotidien`) do not check whether an existing record with the same `id` belongs to another user before overwriting, enabling accidental collisions or malicious overwrites if IDs are guessable.
`rechercherFichiers(_motCle)` ignores the search keyword and effectively returns all files visible to the caller.

`calculerTotaux` and related totals functions treat `#conge` like it can contribute “heures normales” (via `calculerHeuresTravailNormales(entry)`), which is likely a business-logic error (vacation days should typically not add work hours).
Frontend has nested QueryClientProviders with different QueryClient instances (main.tsx and App.tsx), which can lead to confusing cache behavior and duplicate clients.
Frontend PDF export depends on pop-ups and printing a new window; pop-up blockers can prevent PDF generation and there is no direct PDF file blob download.
Journal voice recording does not appear to upload/store audio in the backend (audioUrl is saved as an empty string; recorded audio is only used to set a placeholder transcription message).

AccessControl.getUserRole traps for authenticated-but-unregistered principals; the frontend mitigates this by calling `initializeAccessControl()` on actor creation, but external clients could hit this trap if they skip initialization.
Android-only: after tapping any icon/tab (including bottom navigation and other icons), the app shows a blank white screen; user cannot test on desktop (no computer).

existing_features.title: Internet Identity authentication (login/logout) and persisted sessions
existing_features.description: Provides Internet Identity authentication via a React Context (InternetIdentityProvider), including login/logout, persisted identity loading on mount, and delegation configuration (long TTL). UI surfaces login state and errors.

existing_features.title: Identity-bound backend actor creation with cache reset
existing_features.description: Creates an ICP canister actor configured with the current identity. On identity change, invalidates/refetches React Query caches (except the actor query) to avoid stale or cross-user data. Calls backend `initializeAccessControl()` after authenticated actor creation.

existing_features.title: Role-based access control with admin bootstrap and role assignment
existing_features.description: Motoko access control module assigns the first registered principal as admin, subsequent principals as users, and anonymous callers as guests. Exposes role querying, admin check, and admin-only role assignment; backend methods gate access via `hasPermission` and owner/admin checks.

existing_features.title: User profile setup and persistence
existing_features.description: Allows authenticated users to fetch and save their profile (name, optional email). Frontend forces initial profile setup via a modal when no profile exists for the caller.

existing_features.title: Time entry CRUD (work/vacation/on-call) with detailed fields
existing_features.description: Backend supports creating, updating, deleting, and listing time entries with date, morning/afternoon times, optional on-call (astreinte) time range, meal time, travel time, day type, and description. Frontend wraps these operations in React Query mutations and keeps relevant statistics queries in sync via invalidation.

existing_features.title: Interactive calendar UI for daily entry management
existing_features.description: Monthly calendar view with month navigation and per-day visual indicators. Clicking a day opens a dialog to add/edit time entry data, including time pickers, day type selection, description, and validation ensuring chronological ordering of time ranges.

existing_features.title: On-call (astreinte) handling with separate hour calculations and weekday rules (frontend)
existing_features.description: Frontend computes on-call hours from the precise astreinte time window and applies a business rule where weekday on-call days count both as on-call and as worked days in dashboard and reports summaries.

existing_features.title: Daily media attachments (photos and audio) per calendar day
existing_features.description: Supports uploading and listing media linked to a specific day: photo uploads with drag-and-drop, file validation (type/size), and upload progress; audio recording via MediaRecorder saved as daily media; playback and deletion in the Calendar media tab. Backend stores DailyMediaEntry records and can return all media or filtered photo/audio lists for a day.

existing_features.title: Work journal CRUD with notes, photos, and day type tagging
existing_features.description: Users can create, edit, and delete journal entries with transcription text, written notes, photo attachments (with upload progress and validation), and an optional day-type tag (mutually exclusive selection). Entries are listed with badges and photo previews.

existing_features.title: Dashboard analytics with charts and KPI cards
existing_features.description: Displays monthly KPIs (normal work hours, on-call hours, meal hours, travel hours, worked/vacation/on-call days) and renders charts: weekly bar chart (ISO week buckets), day-type distribution pie chart, and hours distribution pie chart.

existing_features.title: Vacation and on-call day count statistics (backend + frontend)
existing_features.description: Backend computes totals of vacation days and on-call days for a user; frontend fetches these counts with React Query and displays annual totals on the dashboard. Mutations invalidate these stats appropriately.

existing_features.title: Reports view with period selection, summaries, and detailed tables
existing_features.description: Provides a reporting page that filters entries for the current week or current month, computes totals (normal/on-call/meal/travel), and displays a detailed table with per-entry derived hours and day-type badges (including weekday on-call +work indicator).

existing_features.title: CSV export for time reports
existing_features.description: Generates a CSV file client-side for the currently selected report period, including formatted times, derived hours, and annotations for weekday on-call days counted as work+on-call.

existing_features.title: Backend-assisted PDF report data generation and client-side printing
existing_features.description: Frontend requests structured PDF report data from the backend for weekly or monthly periods, then renders an HTML document in a new window and triggers printing to allow users to save as PDF via the browser print dialog.

existing_features.title: Backend totals calculation endpoints
existing_features.description: Backend provides total calculations across entries (overall and per-user, intended per-month/per-week) including normal work, on-call, meal, and travel aggregates.

existing_features.title: Blob storage management mixin for external blobs
existing_features.description: Includes a Motoko mixin for blob lifecycle management: gateway principal authorization refresh, listing and confirming dead blob deletions, blob liveness checks, creation of upload certificates, and cashier cycle refilling guarded by a configured cashier principal.

existing_features.title: File storage endpoints for uploaded files (separate from daily media/journal)
existing_features.description: Backend supports uploading a file object (with metadata and blob content), listing files (admin sees all; users see their own), retrieving by id with authorization checks, and deleting. Provides a placeholder search endpoint.

existing_features.title: HTTP outcalls helper utilities (GET/POST)
existing_features.description: Motoko module to perform HTTP GET/POST requests via IC management canister http_request, with a transform function stripping headers, fixed cycle budget, and user-agent/idempotency headers.

existing_features.title: Camera utility hook (frontend)
existing_features.description: Reusable React hook to manage camera access (start/stop/switch), capture photos to File via canvas, and handle permission/support errors. Present in codebase though not shown as integrated into pages here.

existing_features.title: Build template / scaffolding for ICP + React app (monorepo, deploy scripts, tooling)
existing_features.description: Adds/updates a reusable build template structure for the project, including Dockerfile, ICP deployment config (icp.yaml/canister yamls), workspace package manifests/lockfiles, frontend Vite/Tailwind/shadcn-ui scaffolding, and utility scripts (e.g., prune/resize images) to standardize builds and deployments.

existing_features.title: Fix the Android/mobile navigation regression where tapping any tab/onglet (Dashboard, Calendar, Journal, Reports) results in a blank white screen and makes UI taps non-functional.

Eliminate the nested React Query QueryClientProvider setup that can cause inconsistent cache/context behavior by ensuring the app uses a single QueryClientProvider instance (keep the provider in frontend/src/main.tsx and remove/avoid creating an additional QueryClientProvider in frontend/src/App.tsx).

Add a global error boundary (or equivalent top-level runtime error handling) so that if a page crashes on mobile, the user sees a recoverable in-app error screen with a reset option instead of a blank white screen.

Implement backend-supported user data backup/export and restore/import so a user can recover their personal data across deployments/versions, including user profile, time entries, journal entries, daily media entries, and stored files metadata/links where applicable.

Add an in-app explanation in the restore flow clarifying that restoring pre-Version 32 data is only possible if the data is available via an exported backup file or still exists in canister state from before the upgrade; otherwise the app cannot reconstruct lost data automatically.

Add a repeatable, documented “restart publish” workflow so that after a deployment/publication failure, a developer can re-run the same publish steps safely (idempotent where possible) and get clear English error output.

Fix the Android-only regression where tapping any icon-based UI control (including the bottom navigation tabs and other icon buttons) causes the app to turn into a blank white screen and become non-interactive.

Fix the Android/Chrome runtime crash that occurs immediately when the user taps any icon-based UI control anywhere in the app (e.g., bottom navigation tabs, header icons/buttons), which triggers a DOMException with message similar to: "Failed to execute 'removeChild' on 'Node': The node to be removed is not a child of this node."

Add a small, explicit regression test checklist and in-app debug logging (console only) around tab switching and icon-button clicks to help confirm the fix on Android, without exposing any extra UI to end users.
Update the global crash screen (ErrorBoundary) user-facing text to English (title, description, and buttons), while still showing the underlying error message details for troubleshooting.

new_feature_requests.summary: Add data backup/restore (or migration) so users can recover their previous personal data across deployments/versions (e.g., restore data from before Version 32)
